prompt: Before a month-long rebuild of the billing service, the lead writes a design doc and asks three teams to comment.
tells: writes a design doc and asks three teams to comment
why: Big designs go in writing for review.
trap: Care is warranted, but the act is the written design.

prompt: A year later, no one remembers why the team chose eventual consistency. A new engineer starts writing ADRs for big decisions.
tells: no one remembers why the team chose eventual consistency
trap: It's not debt cleanup; it's documenting why.

prompt: A meeting about a new event system goes in circles. The senior stops it and posts a short RFC so people can comment in writing.
tells: posts a short RFC so people can comment in writing
why: Writing sharpens ideas and lets everyone weigh in.
trap: No decision is made yet, so it's not committing.

prompt: Asked to change how sessions are stored, a mid-level engineer writes a one-page proposal with options and trade-offs before coding.
tells: writes a one-page proposal with options and trade-offs before coding
why: A short written design invites review early.
trap: Clarifying is asking about needs; this is proposing a design.

prompt: In a behavioral interview about influence, a candidate explains they won support for a queue redesign by writing a proposal with data and circulating it.
tells: writing a proposal with data and circulating it
trap: Data helped, but the tool was the written doc.

prompt: After agreeing to drop support for an old browser, the lead records the decision, the reasons and who agreed in the team wiki.
tells: records the decision, the reasons and who agreed
why: Write decisions down so they aren't relitigated or lost.
trap: A decision was made, but the act is recording it.
